subject: Offsite satellite hub and AV credentialing plan for ACME exec workshop
messages:
From: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@acmeinc.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Executive workshop — final venue/AV must-haves

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for walking us through the preliminary agenda. A few operational constraints from our side that will affect venue and AV selection: 

- We'll need an adjacent 'satellite hub' room for secure breakout demos (air-gapped laptop + HSM keybag). No persistent internet on demo machines; vendor will bring a trusted jump host.
- Main plenary (60 pax) requires mixed native AV + hybrid remote—priority is low latency for the CEO Q&A. We prefer low-code STX streaming rather than large-scale Zoom relay if available.
- We will use interpreters for two sessions (EN <> JP). Space for a remote interpreter booth with direct feed to the main audio console is required.
- Network: a separate VLAN for guest Wi‑Fi, a private routed VLAN for demo hardware with firewall rules preloaded, and a site VPN endpoint for our security team to test connectivity in advance.
- Meals: two working lunches plus a plated dinner for exec guests.
- Arrival windows: senior execs arrive 2027-06-06 morning, full workshop 2027-06-07–08.

Can you confirm Redwood's plan for the satellite hub (power, racks, secure storage), interpreter routing, and fallback PSTN dial-in? Also please share any checklist you need completed by our facilities team.

Thanks,
Sarah Connors
Director, Strategic Programs
Acme Inc.

Subject: Re: Executive workshop — final venue/AV must-haves

Team — forwarding ACME's constraints. High-level ask: design a plan that satisfies secure satellite hub requirements while preserving a low-latency hybrid experience. Quick thoughts and owners below: 

- Satellite hub (Laura): 19" rack space for demo units, lockable cabinet, UPS, and on-site secure storage (overnight lockbox). ACME wants no persistent internet on demo machines — we'll build a local jump-host; Karthik to validate VPN endpoint.
- Interpreter routing (Karthik + Marissa): 2x interpreter booths with ISO feed to the main console and stereo mix to the remote stream. Need an inline redundancy path (secondary analog feed + local recorder).
- Low-latency streaming (Karthik): test a two-path stream: primary low-latency STX (SRT or WebRTC) and fallback to Zoom PSTN/Bridge. Also confirm tokenized access control for the remote panel.
- Travel and staging (Hannah): coordinate arrival windows, secure check-in, and concierge for execs. Will compile blocked hotel room lists and a ground-transport SOP.

I'll compile vendor quotes and a condensed ops runbook for ACME's team to sign off tonight. Laura — can you share a venue shortlist and estimate for a secure greenroom footprint? Karthik — need network firewall stanza and HSM handling checklist. Hannah — confirm travel windows & number of airport transfers.

Thanks,
Vivek
Head of Field Ops, Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-05-30T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Executive workshop — final venue/AV must-haves

Vivek — pulled three venues that fit the secure hub requirement:

1) Meridian Conference Center — on-site secure greenroom (20 sqft lockable), 2x booth feeds possible, generator-backed power. Quote attached; vendor can pre-stage UPS and lockboxes. Pros: built-in concierge; Cons: limited adjacent breakout rooms (we'd need to convert a boardroom).

2) Harborview Labs (preferred) — adjacent lab space with independent ingress; clean ethernet runs and isolated patch panels. Good for the air-gapped demo. Requires additional microphone bridges for plenary.

3) The Old Foundry — unique layout, better catering, but will need a temporary rack and certified electrician for HSM power draw.

Estimated additional AV + security uplift per venue: $6,500–$12,000 depending on temporary rack & on-site network engineering. I've attached a vendor quote (line items included). If ACME wants the Harborview Lab, Osprey Events can lock it for 06/06–06/08 with early load-in on 06/05.

Laura Bennett
Senior Events Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Executive workshop — final venue/AV must-haves

Notes on technical checklist (draft) — please comment inline or add to the Drive doc: https://drive.google.com/open?id=acme-exec-workshop-plan

- Satellite hub: 2x dedicated AC circuits, 1x 8U lockable rack, UPS N+1, labeled power runs. No outbound default route on demo machines. Local jump-host with a whitelist for the HSM serial/IP. We will bring a hardware HSM keybag for signing tests; ACME security to approve on-site handling protocol (I can draft).
- Network: pre-provisioned VPN endpoint (wireguard) for Redwood test accounts; site must provide port-forwarding for SSH test <-> jump-host during staging window. Firewall rules: deny internet egress for the demo VLAN except for a controlled NAT box.
- Streaming: primary WebRTC session (TURN/STUN) across a prioritized ISP; fallback SRT to Redwood bridge + PSTN dial-in. Configure 3x redundant encoders (2x software, 1x hardware).
- Interpreter booth: direct AES/analog split to console + 2x headphone amps with independent monitor mixes. Ensure ISO mic preamps near booth and feed to remote stream with independent codec.
- Recording & evidence: local recorder with signed manifests and an SHA256 checksum of recorded assets for ACME compliance.

I'll attach a small HSM handling checklist and the firewall stanza this afternoon.

Karthik
Director, Solutions Engineering

- Headcount: ACME confirmed 58 in-person + 12 remote exec seats. Interpreters: 2 onsite + 1 remote backup.
- Travel: 4 execs on 06/06 AM arrival (SFO), 6 national guests on 06/06 PM, local staff arriving 06/05 for load-in. I'll coordinate car pick-ups (4x sedans, 2x SUV for equipment).
- Hotels: holding block at The Meridian (10 rooms) and Harborview Suites (12 rooms) — prefer Harborview for proximity to the lab.
- Catering: two working boxed lunches (no hot buffets due to space) and plated dinner on 06/06. Dietary restrictions: 4 vegetarian, 2 pescatarian, 1 gluten-free.

Subject: Re: Executive workshop — final venue/AV must-haves — plan and next steps

Sarah — thanks for the clear requirements. Proposed plan (summary):

1) Venue: Harborview Labs (recommended) — allows independent lab ingress and simplifies the air-gap requirement. Osprey to confirm venue booking by 06/03.
2) Satellite hub: we'll provision an 8U lockable rack, UPS, and temporary local jump-host. HSM custodian will be named by Redwood (Ben Carter) and we'll send ACME's facilities the badge list by 06/03.
3) Streaming & redundancy: primary WebRTC low-latency path + SRT fallback; local hardware encoder + two software encoders. PSTN dial-in available as emergency fallback.
4) Interpreter routing: 2x onsite booths with AES split to console and independent mixes; remote interpreter via dedicated codec feed.
5) Security & evidence: local recorder + checksum manifest; firewall stanza and WireGuard test credentials to be provided to ACME security 48 hours prior to load-in.

Attachments: vendor_quote_on_site_av.xlsx, acme_site_requirements_v2.pdf, satellite-hub-network-map.png.

Immediate asks for ACME:
- Final headcount and dietary confirmations by 06/03.
- Approval to proceed with Harborview booking (Osprey will issue T&C).
- Confirmation that ACME security approves a single HSM custodian (Ben Carter) and provides badge access on 06/05.

If no major objections, we'll issue a concise ops runbook and a one-page site-staging checklist tomorrow morning.

Best,
Vivek
Head of Field Ops, Redwood Inference
